Objective
Learn when a negative factor reverses an inequality, how to isolate the variable, and how to check each answer.
Number line
Three is less than five. After multiplying by negative one, negative three is greater than negative five; order flips.
Rule
Addition and subtraction preserve comparisons. Negative multiplication or division reverses them; positive factors do not.
Example 1
Negative three x greater than twelve means x less than negative four. Check x equals negative five: fifteen exceeds twelve.
Example 2
If x divided by negative five is at most two, multiply by negative five and reverse: x is at least negative ten.
Distribute
Negative two times x minus one at least eight becomes negative two x plus two at least eight, then x at most negative three.
Multi-step
Negative four x plus seven less than nineteen becomes negative four x less than twelve, then x greater than negative three.
Both sides
Two x minus five less than negative x plus seven becomes three x less than twelve, so x less than four.
Context
Fifty liters minus three point five liters each minute must exceed fifteen liters; time is less than ten minutes.
Boundaries
Strict less than excludes the boundary and uses an open circle. Less than or equal includes it and uses a closed circle.
Check
Simplify, isolate, reverse only after a negative multiplication or division, then test a value in the original inequality.
Recap
Negative five x less than ten gives x greater than negative two. Practice eighteen questions, then take the five-question test.
